newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Protesters disrupt Philippine Congress session.
newsitem.headline: Protesters disrupt Philippine Congress session.

text.p: Dozens of protesters opposed to a second term for Philippine President Fidel Ramos disrupted a session of the Congress on Monday by chanting slogans comparing Ramos to late dictator Ferdinand Marcos.
"Ramos, Marcos, one and the same," chanted members of the Nationalist Patriotic Alliance, a militant leftist group, as guards dragged them out of the gallery of the House of Representatives.
The rowdy protest prompted legislators to adjourn their session.
One of the bills pending in the legislature calls for the country's 10-year-old constitution to be amended to allow Ramos to run for re-election when his current six-year term expires next year.

The constitution limits a president to only one term to prevent the rise of another Marcos, who ruled the country with an iron fist for 20 years until he was ousted in a 1986 popular revolt. Marcos died in exile in Hawaii in 1989.

Ramos has said he will step down when his term ends but his supporters are demanding he be allowed to run again to ensure the continuity of his reform programme, which has breathed life into a once-stagnant economy.

Congressional sources said the legislative proposal had a fair chance of passing the Lower House which is controlled by a pro-Ramos coalition but could find the sailing rough in the opposition-held Senate.

The proposal calls for the convening of the two houses of Congress into a joint session to draft amendments to the constitution. Proposed amendments, however, need to be approved by Filipino voters in a nationwide referendum.
